top_issues: How to read this explainer is dense jargon (on-chain/reserve/collateral/promised) for a first-timer; it sits under the balance, not in the first glance.
Instant spend ceiling (send up to $175 / receive up to $250) is small, easy-to-miss text under the three action buttons, not tied to the balance bar.
The balanced Accounts panel runs far right, far from the balance it reconciles, weakening at-a-glance comprehension on wide screens.
fixes: Keep the explainer but add a short plain-language line first: 'Green = you own it now. Violet = a partner promised it.' before the technical terms.
Promote the instant-send ceiling into the Pay button sub-label (e.g. 'Pay — up to 175 instantly').
Pull a compact 'accounts reconciliation' strip directly under the total balance, or collapse the far-right panel into the main column.

top_issues: Two bars labelled 'This payment' and 'your account with H1' sit side-by-side and read as duplicates to a first-timer; the before/after story needs one label.
Fee stated as 'under 0.01 USDC' and '1 bps' is technically precise but not a flat, copyable number.
The 'To' field shows a raw 0x hash under the name H2 — useful for verification but visually noisy on the primary action screen.
fixes: Merge into one 'After this payment' bar with Before/After markers, and add a 'your balance after: 90.00' line.
Show a literal fee: 'Fee ≈ 0.008 USDC (0.08%)' so the cost is pastable.
Collapse the full hash behind a 'view' affordance, showing only H2 + a short '0x92c2…cbf0'.

top_issues: Proof hash is truncated to 0x525d2ae3…f954 with no 'copy' affordance on the hash itself.
The 'Copy receipt / Download / Print / PDF' row has four equal buttons, diluting the single most likely action (forward to the payer/client).
'Verified by your runtime' is a strong trust cue but placed below the proof where a skeptical user may stop reading.
fixes: Add a copy icon directly beside the proof hash and a 'copy full proof' at the row level.
Make 'Copy receipt' the primary filled action, with Download and Print/PDF as secondary ghost buttons.
Move the 'verified by your runtime' line just under the settlement time/frame so the proof chain reads top-down.

top_issues: 'Amount optional' and '25.50 capacity via H1' are detached: capacity appears top-right of the amount card yet the note says the sender chooses the route.
'What is this for?' is the only note affordance; it reads as a throwaway comment field, not the invoice line a freelancer needs.
No denomination or expiry on the QR/payment link, so a shared link can be reused or misinterpreted.
fixes: Put 'capacity 25.50 via H1' inline with the amount field and show the effective cap in the amount unit.
Rename the note to 'What is this for? (appears on receipt)' so it is clearly part of the record.
Add an optional 'expires' and 'maximum amount' control so shared links are bound to a value and window.

top_issues: The order book labels lots in bps (2.505.0000 → size 25.500) with no 'equivalent @ 1 USDC' so Anya must mentally convert.
'Gross receive: 0.039992 WETH before fees' then a sentence on collateral — the fee-yield is explained in prose, not arithmetic.
Lot rounding of '0.000004 USDC stays with you' reads as trivia, not an impact on receive.
fixes: Add a per-lot row '≈ $X' so size converts to dollars at a glance.
Replace prose with a 3-line arithmetic block: gross − hub fee − collateral buffer = net you receive.
Show lot rounding as a small '+0.000004 USDC back' line inside the receive field rather than a standalone term.

top_issues: The Legs panel (1 Testnet / 2 Tron / 3 Clear) is genuinely excellent but visually competes with a dense left column and a buried 'zero credit' warning.
'Prepare incoming capacity before swapping' is red lowercase under the CTA — the single most consequential action is the least prominent element.
Settlement 'Atomic: both legs or neither' is good, but the collateral/credit interplay ('0 WETH + 0.000798 WETH') is hard to parse in one line.
fixes: Give the Legs panel more visual weight (larger, with per-leg status) and make it the top-right anchor.
Promote the capacity warning to a full-width amber banner above the swap button.
Break the collateral line into two rows: 'collateral you provide' and 'credit you would extend' with the resulting spread.

top_issues: The legend (secured/promised/you owe/credit room/in flight) hangs over the USDC card but the WETH card below has no legend, so colors lose their key.
'90.00' balance is large but the critical 'They owe you uncovered: $90.00' sits in the right panel, separated from the bar that shows it.
Dispute is a small text button under 'If you dispute, they answer within 1d' — not a first-class action for the security-maximalist persona.
fixes: Repeats a compact legend on each lane card, or move the legend into the This Account panel as a persistent key.
Place 'They owe you uncovered $90.00' directly under the USDC bar, in the same lane, for one-glance risk.
Upgrade Dispute to a full-width outlined button with the 1d window in its label.

top_issues: The detail panel mirrors the selected row (both show -25.00, To H2, frame, proof) producing strong duplication; the panel adds only time + frames count.
Filters (Payments/Swaps/Settlement/Accounts) mix event types with trade types, so 'settlement' and 'swap' can be confused.
Export CSV is a plain text link, top-center, easy to miss and with no format/scope cue.
fixes: Make the detail panel additive: show proof, frames, and a map/route — elements not present in the row.
Clarify filters: split 'Payments' vs 'Transfers', and label 'Settlement' as 'Settlements'.
Give Export CSV a labeled button and a subtle 'export all 7 movements (JSON/CSV)' scope.

top_issues: Same duplication as 07: the detail card restates the row without adding a unique visual (route map, signatures, hash ladder).
Proof is truncated again with no copy affordance on the hash.
'2 committed entries' doesn't expand to show the two signed frames — a treasurer wants the actual frame content.
fixes: Add a route/signature visual and an expandable 'show the 2 committed frames' row in the detail card.
Add copy + 'copy full proof' beside the proof hash.
Render the two frame entries as a small table (frame #, signer, hash) so the export is inspectable in-app.

top_issues: The bar-scale demo ($1,284,500) uses a real-ish figure but the 'AT THIS SCALE' bars overlap the explanation and the $100–$1000 rows saturate the same width, weakening the lesson.
Two distinct 'Dark' toggles (Theme / Material) plus a Material name (Obsidian/Private bank/Terminal) creates redundant, near-synonymous darkness controls.
Runtime id, frame, and vault block crowd the bottom; the imported-vault 'managed' status is easy to read as a warning.
fixes: Animate the scale demo, or use a clean 3-row example (100 / 1,000 / 10,000) without overlap so the log-then-linear truth is visible.
Merge Theme+Material into one 'Appearance — Dark/Light + Material' group, removing the duplicate toggle.
Label the Vault block 'imported vault — managed (ok)' in positive green, not neutral; wrap runtime id/frame in a details disclosure.

top_issues: From/To cards show identical labels (Wallet/0.00, Reserve/40.00, Account/150.00) so a first-timer cannot tell that pressing a destination is selection vs a value.
Both WETH and USDC appear unlabeled in the From/To cards, but the amount card shows only USDC — the asset being moved is ambiguous.
'Fund you through H1' in the What-Happens panel reads as instruction not consequence.
fixes: Add a source ('') vs dest ('→') affordance on the cards, and show the selected card with a check.
Place an explicit asset selector above the amount so From/To always align to the chosen token; default to the asset in the selected From card.
Reword helper to outcome: 'Result: Reserve posts collateral on-chain; the Account can be used instantly.'

top_issues: 'Where your money stands' is the strongest element but sits below the fold of a screen whose primary value is navigation.
Needs attention shows 'Nothing waiting on you' — a positive state rendered as a near-empty box, which reads as a bug more than a clean bill.
The Accounts card (H1, 3 lanes, 15 frames) doesn't summarize risk; it only lists counts.
fixes: Move the money-standings summary to the top so the safe/at-risk split is the first read.
Replace the empty 'Needs attention' box with a single green line: '✓ Nothing needs you — all accounts settled.'
Add an at-risk figure to the Accounts card (e.g., 'at risk 25.50') so the card is decision-ready.

top_issues: Faucet and On-chain Wallet occupy equal weight, but on Mainnet the faucet is irrelevant — the screen is testnet-heavy for a production product.
Three 'Receive…' buttons (Extend credit / Receive USDC from H1 / USDC to my on-chain wallet…) have rising opacity that reads as a gradient, not a hierarchy.
Debts panel is tiny and 'No debts' is arguably the most important safety signal, yet it's the most cramped element.
fixes: Gate the faucet behind a testnet flag so Mainnet shows a clean on-chain wallet.
Give distinct states to the three receive actions: one primary, the rest ghost, with explicit 'from H1' vs 'from on-chain' labels.
Make the Debts panel a confident '✓ No debts on the Depository' with more breathing room.

top_issues: Interest 'you ask: 100 bps = 100% per term' is a legitimately alarming-looking figure; the bps→percent conversion is shown but not contextualised.
The '= 100% per term' sideline is right-aligned and reads as a formula, not an explanation.
No risk-return cue (e.g., 'this is a hub promise, not on-chain') on the lend offer, which a skeptical lender needs before committing.
fixes: Show a worked example: 'Lend 100 USDC for 1 day → receive ~100.27 USDC' instead of only bps/percent.
Add a one-line risk note above the CTA: 'This earns interest at a hub's promise — it is not on-chain collateral.'
Label the term selector with the actual dates (e.g., '1 day — ends 04:50 tomorrow') so yield is time-bound.

top_issues: The screen is mostly explanatory prose about quorums and boards with no interactive control to actually rotate a signer or change a threshold.
'Take control of another entity' is empty with no path to begin, so a real user hits a dead end.
Kind 'Self-issued (its id is the hash of its board)' is correct but reads as circular to a newcomer.
fixes: Add a real action: 'Add signer / change threshold' with a numeric stepper and a signature-required warning.
Give the Take-control panel a 'start' state or hide it entirely until another entity lists your signer.
Clarify kind: 'Self-issued — your entity address is derived from this board (immutable).'

top_issues: This is the strongest trust screen in the set; weakness is only in the Per-counterparty panel, which shows '$90.00 at risk' but the matching bar is the main balance's violet segment, not a dedicated lane.
'Save evidence bundle' is the natural Ravi/Kenji exit but it's a plain outlined button at the bottom, not a prominent export.
The Keys/Claims/Ledger blocks are dense; a non-technical reader may bounce before the 'enforceable right now' message lands.
fixes: Add a small 'at risk' bar directly in the Per-counterparty panel so the risk figure has its own scale visual.
Make 'Save evidence bundle' a primary filled button with a sub-label 'JSON + PDF for your board'.
Keep the Keys/Ledger blocks but move the plain-language 'Green = yours, Violet = promised' summary to the top of the screen.

top_issues: The account-lane table shows 'CREDIT OUT 115.50.0' and 'CREDIT RECV 25.50' — a likely typo/concatenation ('115.50.0') that undermines trust in a pro tool.
Top summary cards ($130.00 / $40 / $90 / $150.00-$275.75) are only loosely labelled; 'on-chain $130' vs '$90' vs '$150-$275' isn't reconciled at a glance.
The Desks table columns (position/secure/promised/you owe) are dense and the legend is relegated under the table, so first-time Marcus squints.
fixes: Fix the '115.50.0' typo; render credit lines as clean numbers ('115.50').
Label the four summary cards explicitly: 'Balance', 'On-chain', 'At risk', 'Credit range' with a one-line cast of account vs reserve.
Push the legend above the table and bold the 'at risk' column so risk pops first.

top_issues: The palette is a keyboard-first power feature but lacks a visible search field and shows no shortcuts (⌘K is implied, not shown).
Items are grouped with muted descriptions but no grouping headers, so the list reads as one flat menu.
The overlay dims the Desk but leaves the right-hand order book fully bright, splitting attention.
fixes: Add a search input ('Search or jump…') and list the ⌘K shortcut in the top-right of the palette.
Insert subtle section headers (Home / Finance / Trust) between the item groups.
Dim the whole backdrop evenly so the palette is the only focus.

overall.verdict: The xln desktop-dark set is a genuinely strong, coherent fintech UI whose single-absolute-scale bars make risk and guarantee legible at a glance — a real differentiator. It is held back mainly by the absence of mobile proof, no first-class invoice flow, and a dense technical register that trips first-timers on advanced surfaces.
priority_fixes: Prove one-hand mobile usability — add mobile screenshots and a compact layout with large tap targets (satisfies Lena, lifts the responsive score across the board).
Add a dedicated invoice flow — create, number, due date, line items, share link, settle → forwardable receipt (satisfies Sofia).
Surface the first-run plain-language guide on Home so reserve/account/collateral map to 'yours vs promised' before jargon (satisfies Maya and Dmitri).
Show cross-network fees as a flat dollar amount in addition to bps on Swap/Send (satisfies Fatima, clarifies Anya).
Promote Dispute to a first-class screen from the Account view, with the challenge window and evidence bundle in one place (satisfies Kenji and Ravi).

blockers: Home bar legend still uses reserve/collateral/credit-line jargon in the first glance (01-home)
Move screen (10) doesn't explain reserve vs account to a first-timer

personas.name: Tomasz

blockers: Account view (06) legend sits over USDC but not the WETH lane below, so the key is lost on the second lane

personas.name: Anya
personas.verdict: The order book, limit price, live fills and history are all here — I could swap 1 ETH at a fair price and see exactly why.
blockers: Book rows are in bps, not dollars, so I convert mentally (05-swap)
Cross-network legs (05b) are strong but the fee is bps, not a flat number

personas.verdict: Sovereignty tells me what is enforceable right now and lets me save an evidence bundle — that's a board-ready export.

Detail view (08) doesn't expand the two committed frames for inspection

personas.name: Kenji

Evidence bundle export is secondary (15), not tied to a dispute

personas.name: Lena

personas.name: Marcus

blockers: The Desk column 'CREDIT OUT 115.50.0' shows a concatenation artifact (16-desk) that undermines trust

personas.verdict: The Legs breakdown made the cross-chain path finally make sense, and the fee is shown — though only in bps.

personas.verdict: From the screens alone, this is a product that tells you exactly what is yours versus what is promised — and that's rare.

What backs a hub's promise isn't fully stated in a single glance
